newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to extradite Colombian drug lord to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to extradite Colombian drug lord to U.S.

text.p: Venezuela's Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that suspected Colombian drug kingpin Justo Pastor Perafan should be extradited to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.

"The Supreme Court decided in its session today to rule in favour of extraditing the Colombian Justo Pastor Perafan to the United States for the crime of drug trafficking," Supreme Court vice-President Ismael Rodriguez Salazar.
Perafan, believed to be the last Colombian drug billionaire not in jail or dead, was captured in April by Venezuelan authorities in the western town of San Cristobal, across the border from Colombia.
Perafan had asked to be sent back to Colombia, which had also lodged an extradition request with Venezuela.
But many legal experts, and even Colombia's police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano, have said he would face a tougher sentence in the United States.

Perafan, who was using an alias and had undergone plastic surgery and hair implants to change his appearance, was said to be one of the wealthiest Colombian cocaine lords still on the run with a personal fortune estimated at $12 billion.
